(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.
These appeals arise out of a judgment and award dated 08.01.2021 passed in MVC No.446 of 2018 by the learned XII Additional District and SessionS Judge, Belagavi, sitting at Gokak.

2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of these appeals are as follows:
3. On 01.11.2017 the petitioner/claimant was doing the cleaner work on the tractor bearing registration number KA-49/T-9509 and trailer KA-48/T-6991 as per the instructions of respondent No.3, who is the owner of the tractor and trailer.

At that time, the driver of the offending school bus bearing registration No.KA-49/1121 belonging to respondent No.1 and NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR insured with the insurance company i.e., Barthi AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd. came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the tractor.

entities.text: Barthi AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner was aged about 25 years as of the date of accident and earning 10,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has become disabled and not in a position to do work.

The petitioner filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act', for short) seeking compensation on the account of injuries sustained in the road traffic The Manager, Bharati Axa General ... vs Krishna @ Krishnaji Vithal Kaparatti on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111703266/
3 accident.

entities.text: Manager, Bharati Axa General ... vs Krishna @ Krishnaji Vithal Kaparatti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
4. Notice was issued to the owner of the school bus.
Despite service of notice, the owner of the offending bus remained unrepresented and was placed exparte.
5. The insurance company of the bus filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

On the other hand, there was a negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor and trailer and the driver of the tractor and trailer was not holding an effective driving NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR licence to drive the tractor and trailer.

Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition against the Bharati AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd.
6.

entities.text: Bharati AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The owner of the tractor and trailer-respondent No.3, though appeared through counsel, he did not file statement of objections.

7. Respondent No.4, National Insurance Company, filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the school bus.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition against the it.
8. The Tribunal based on the pleadings of the parties framed the relevant issues.
9. The petitioner to substantiate his case examined himself as PW.1, examined two witnesses as PWs.2 and PW.3 and marked 105 documents as Exhibit P1 to 105.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR 10.

The Tribunal after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded a compensation of 9,42,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e. the owner and the insurance company of the school bus are jointly and severally liable to pay the said amount and directed the insurance company to deposit the said amount.
11.

The petitioner being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation filed appeal in MFA No.101578 of 2021 and the insurance company of the school bus filed appeal in MFA No.100403 of 2021 challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the learned counsel for insurance company of the school bus.
13.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner in order to prove the disability examined the Doctors as PW.2 and PW.3.

They have issued a disability certificate stating that the claimant has suffered disability to NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR the extent of 40% whereas the The Manager, Bharati Axa General ... vs Krishna @ Krishnaji Vithal Kaparatti on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111703266/
4 Tribunal has assessed the disability at 25% which is on the lower side.

entities.text: Manager, Bharati Axa General ... vs Krishna @ Krishnaji Vithal Kaparatti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submits that the compensation awarded on the other heads by the Tribunal is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds he prays to allow the appeal filed by the petitioner and to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurance company.
14. The learned counsel for the insurance company of the school bus submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is exorbitant.
He submits that the disability assessed by the tribunal at 25% is on the higher side.
He also submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the other heads is also on higher side.
Hence, on these ground he prays to allow the appeal filed by the insurance company and to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioner.

15. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
16.
The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR 17.
There is no dispute regarding the petitioner having met with an accident and sustaining injuries.
The petitioner to prove that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the school bus produced the charge sheet marked as Exhibit P7.
The Tribunal was justified in recording the finding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the school bus.

18. Regarding Quantum: The petitioner contended that he was a cleaner and getting an income of 10,000/- per month and because of the injuries sustained, the petitioner is unable to carry out day to day work.

In support of his contention, he has examined the doctors as PW2 and PW3 who have opined that they have examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically and issued disability certificate marked as Ex P.92 and Exhibit P.104.
19.

PW.2 is the doctor who has issued the disability certificate stating that the petitioner has suffered 40% disability and PW.3 is a dental surgeon who has deposed that the petitioner has lost 9 teeth and assessed the disability at 18%.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3597 HC-KAR Both the Doctors have treated the petitioner.
Hence, one third of the disability has to be assessed.
20. From the perusal of the evidence of PW2 and PW3, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 25% to the whole body which is on a higher side.
The same needs to be reduced.
Accordingly, it is reduced from 25% to 18%.
21. The petitioner has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, this Court reassess the notional income at 10,250/- as the accident is of 2017.
The petitioner is aged about 35 years and the multiplier applicable to his age group is 16 as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation1.

ORDER i.
The appeal filed by the petitioner in MFA No.101578/2021 is dismissed.
ii. MFA No.100403/2021 filed by the Insurance Company is allowed.

sitting at Gokak is modified.
